summary: Adaptive linger amplification on streaming resume causing burst p99 latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Dedicated in us-east (ChorusAI) reported intermittent p95/p99 spikes for short streaming requests after sessions resume from brief idle windows. Spikes started 2026-03-09 ~18:00 UTC and correlate with many short streams (single-turn prompts) that reconnect quickly.

Impact:
- Multiple production tenants observed p99 jump from ~120ms to 800-1200ms for short streaming requests.
- Client-side timeouts increased; several 504s reported by customer.
- Affects user-facing product features (chat quick-reply) for ChorusAI customers on dedicated capacity.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (us-east), serving runtime v2.8.3, continuous-batcher enabled with adaptive_linger and priority_decay settings.
- Traffic pattern: many short-lived streaming connections with pauses of 200-800ms between messages.

Steps to reproduce (customer recipe):
1) Open 200 short streaming connections at 10r/s total QPS, each sends a 10-token prompt then pauses 400ms and resumes.
2) Observe latency distribution using the request_id returned by the streaming handshake.
3) Reproduce with model gpt-small-v1 pinned.

Observed behavior:
- p95 and p99 increase in bursts when many streams resume concurrently.
- Traces show linger window decisions expanding for resumed connections (linger accrued to >120ms) before flush.
- KV-cache hits are high; not a cold-cache symptom.

Expected behavior:
- Short resume bursts should be flushed promptly, maintaining p95/p99 within baseline.

Logs & dashboards (examples):
- Metrics: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/continuous/batcher?orgId=1&from=now-6h&to=now
- Trace example: trace-id=3a8f7b2d (attached in upload)
- Sample worker log excerpt: "[batcher] adaptive_linger_ms adjusted from 12 -> 96 for tenant=chorusai request=..."

Initial hypothesis:
Adaptive linger algorithm plus priority_decay interacts poorly with stream-resume patterns. When a connection resumes after a short idle, the algorithm temporarily increases its linger estimate to favor coalescing; concurrent resumes create a feedback loop where linger amplifies across microbatches, causing delayed flushes and p99 spikes. Throttling/backpressure and per-connection rate smoothing exacerbate the effect.

investigation_notes: Reproduction: traffic replay with 200 concurrent short streams reproduced p99 from 130ms -> 1.1s in ~6 minutes.
Trace analysis: worker flush times increased; microbatch sizes were slightly larger than normal but not enough to justify the added latency.
Batcher config: adaptive_linger_enabled=true, adaptive_linger_base_ms=8, adaptive_linger_max_ms=200, priority_decay_ms=3000.

Root cause theory: adaptive algorithm increases linger when it detects repeated short pauses; priority_decay keeps resumed streams in lower scheduling priority long enough for their linger to compound across multiple resume cycles. When many streams resume concurrently the batcher amplifies the window to maximize coalescing, but this creates tail latency for short requests.
Additional contributing factors: per-connection token pacing and RPC backpressure signals delayed early flushes for streams resuming mid-window.
Temporary mitigation validated: setting max_linger_ms=30 and reducing priority_decay_ms to 800ms for streaming routes restored p99 to ~150-170ms under replay.
Telemetry: added a new gauge 'batcher.linger_amplification' to track how often adaptive_linger increases >4x over base for a tenant.
Related issues reviewed: SUP-93177 (staggered flush resonance) - similar amplification phenomenon but different trigger; SUP-9023 (idle threshold drift) - useful patterns for detection.
resolution: Workaround and permanent fix deployed. Workaround: applied configuration change in us-east dedicated pool on 2026-03-11 02:05 UTC - max_linger_ms enforced at 30ms and priority_decay_ms set to 800ms for streaming routes; customer confirmed reduction in errors. Permanent fix: merged PR github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2410 which implements a resume-aware adaptive_linger decay and global amplification cap. Rollout timeline: canary 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC -> regional rollout us-east 2026-03-12 05:00 UTC -> global 2026-03-13 01:00 UTC. Post-deploy monitoring shows p99 back to baseline for replay tests. Follow-up: add automated alert when batcher.linger_amplification > 0.05 for 5m and document recommended batcher config for dedicated streaming tenants in Confluence runbook. Closing notes: keep issue open for 72h of steady-state monitoring before final close.
